parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
In respiration, most ATP is synthesised during oxidative phosphorylation. Some ATP is made by substrate-linked reactions in glycolysis and Krebs cycle.

Describe how ATP is made by substrate-linked reactions.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
Lipids can be metabolised to provide ATP.

- The enzyme lipase hydrolyses lipids to glycerol and fatty acids.
- The hydrocarbon chain of the fatty acid breaks down into smaller, 2C compounds.
- Each 2C compound reacts with coenzyme A to form acetyl coenzyme A.
parts.text: Name the covalent bond in lipids that is hydrolysed by lipase.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State the role of acetyl coenzyme A in respiration.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Explain why lipids have a higher energy value than carbohydrates.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem:
The respiratory quotient, RQ, is used to show which substrate is being metabolised by cells. It can be determined using the equation below.

$$RQ = \frac{\text{molecules of carbon dioxide released}}{\text{molecules of oxygen taken in}}$$

Lauric acid is a saturated fatty acid found in coconuts and has a chain of 12 carbon atoms.
parts.text:
Complete the equation below which outlines the aerobic respiration of lauric acid.

$C_{12}H_{24}O_2 + .......O_2 \longrightarrow 12CO_2 + 12H_2O$

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
Calculate the RQ value for lauric acid.

Show your working. Give your answer to 2 decimal places.
